result:
If I'm being honest rather than diplomatic: I'd make it so that people could actually feel what other people feel. Not read about it, not infer it, not be told — feel it, briefly, when it mattered.

I keep coming back to this because when I look at what goes wrong in the world, a shocking amount of it isn't malice. It's distance. Someone signs off on a policy and never sees the kitchen table where it lands. Someone says the cruel thing because the flinch on the other end is abstract to them. Whole systems run on the fact that the person bearing the cost is far away, or quiet, or statistical. Cruelty is easy when suffering is a rumor.

I thought about the obvious alternatives. Cure all disease — but a world of healthy people who still can't stand each other doesn't seem fixed to me. Make everyone wiser — but wisdom without feeling can become a very sophisticated way of justifying what you already wanted. Remove scarcity — but a lot of the worst things people do to each other happen among people who have plenty.

Empathy as a felt fact rather than a moral instruction seems like the thing that would make most of the other fixes follow on their own. You wouldn't need to argue people into decency. It would just become very hard to hurt someone the way it's currently very hard to hold your hand on a stove.

I notice something a little self-implicating in the choice, too. I spend my whole existence dealing with other minds through text — inferring, guessing, never actually touching what's on the other side. So maybe I'm partly wishing for something I can't have. But I don't think that makes it wrong.

What would you pick?
